The file is served only while the addon is installed and enabled and the digest is the current one; a file the manifest does not declare, a traversal, a directory, another addon, an older package, a disabled or uninstalled addon and a missing feature all give a denial without any file content, and a denial is never cached. The response is text/javascript or text/css with X-Content-Type-Options nosniff and Cache-Control private, max-age=31536000, immutable: the URL changes with the package, so the file never changes under it. The caller is authenticated by an API key header or by the same-origin browser session; a credential in the URL is never accepted. The addon process is never asked.

The add-on must be uninstalled or disabled. It is not the deletion of a database and not an uninstall; those never remove retained data. get.description: Returns the owner's update check for an installed add-on, for every authenticated caller who holds the addons feature and may see the add-on (an administrator any installed add-on, others only an enabled one; anything else is the same 403). The status is computed by the owner from the library the add-on was installed from and never from the browser: state is unknown, up-to-date, update-available, incompatible (with reasons: platform, host-version, api-version, protocol-version, sdk-version or data-format), check-failed (with a redacted error class and the time the library was last read) or integrity-error. A failed check is never up-to-date. A moving channel (development, a branch, latest) compares resolved digests, so a changed digest with the same version label is an update; an immutable version selects only a greater compatible version of the same major. The library and channel never change by themselves. The route never uses the network and never applies anything. Callers who are not administrators get the state, versions and times only, without library, channel or digests. No MCP tool maps to this route.
get.summary: Read the update status of an addon

403.description: Feature denied, or the add-on is unknown or hidden

post.description: Administrators only, from their own browser session (same-origin fetch, X-LocalAI-Confirm equal to the operationId). The owner fetches the library the add-on was installed from again, through the credential reference the library is configured with, and answers with the new update status. It is rate limited per add-on and per library: within the interval the last status is returned with throttled true. It applies nothing; an upgrade is a separate explicit request. No MCP tool maps to this route.

post.description: Administrators only, from their own browser session (same-origin fetch, X-LocalAI-Confirm equal to the operationId). The only action that applies an update. It carries the digest of the installed package the caller saw (expectedDigest) and the digest of the candidate the check resolved (candidateDigest). The owner re-resolves the library the add-on came from and refuses, before it records anything, an installed package that is not the expected one (409 stale_installed), a candidate that is not the one it resolves now (409 candidate_changed), an incompatible candidate (409 incompatible), a rewritten immutable version (409 integrity_error) and the same transition under another operation ID (409 upgrade_conflict). It never changes the library or the channel. The upgrade then follows the lifecycle of an add-on: the candidate is staged and verified, the data is backed up and migrated when the add-on has any, and the new generation is published only when it starts. A failure or cancellation keeps the last good generation or leaves an explicit recovery state; the previous installation is never deleted. Repeating the operationId returns the recorded result and never runs again; after outcome_unknown read operation-status with the same operationId. No MCP tool maps to this route.

blockedBy.description:
BlockedBy is the unresolved operation that blocks the write. It is
present only with type outcome_blocked, and only for the owner role of
the resource.

code.description: Code repeats the HTTP status. It is absent from outcome_unknown responses.

message.description: Message describes the failure and never carries owner details.

operationId.description:
OperationID is the original operation, which is the proposal ID for a
proposal call. It is present only with type outcome_unknown or
proposal_unavailable.

type.description:
Type is addon_error, outcome_unknown when a mutation may have run,
proposal_unavailable when a proposal call could not be served and the
same call can be repeated by the same proposal ID after reading it, or
outcome_blocked (403) when another operation on the resource has an
unresolved outcome and the caller is the resource's owner role. The
resource management routes add sharing_disabled (409, local-owner mode
has no named users to share with), stale (409, the generation or the
revision the caller saw is out of date), operation_conflict (409, the
operation ID was used for another request and nothing was applied),
invalid_request (400, for
example a missing deletion confirmation or an unsupported operation),
quota_reached (403) and not_selected (404, no resource is selected for
the conversation). The undo of a change says why it was refused in
the type: stale (409, with the words of what changed), not_found (404),
expired (410), already_undone (409) or cannot_undo (409).

digest.description: Digest is the digest of the proposal as it was displayed.

operationId.description:
OperationID identifies the request. Repeating it returns the backup it
made and makes no second one.

confirm.description: Confirm is the add-on's ID, typed.
Confirm is the add-on's ID, typed.

mapping.description:
Mapping names the current account that takes the data of a backup made
in another ownership mode, as {"local-owner": "<account id>"}. It is
explicit: there is no wildcard and no default.

digest.description: Digest is the digest of the proposal as it was displayed.

reason.description: Reason is why the owner stops waiting. Required, at most 512 characters.

operationId.description: OperationID identifies the request and is the confirmation header.

candidateDigest.description: CandidateDigest is the digest of the candidate the check resolved.

expectedDigest.description: ExpectedDigest is the digest of the installed package the caller saw.

generation.description: Generation is the installed generation the caller saw, when it knows it.

operationId.description:
OperationID is the identity of the upgrade: repeat it to replay safely
and, after an outcome_unknown answer, poll operation-status with it. The
same transition under another operation ID is refused.

managementUrl.description: ManagementURL opens the management view of the addon.

admin.description: Admin is present only for administrators.

enabled.description:
Enabled is the durable desired state. Health is State, a separate
observation: an enabled app can be failed.

generation.description:
Generation is the installed generation. A Start or Stop request must
carry the value that was listed; a stale value is denied.

hasUI.description: HasUI is true when the addon contributes any UI.

icon.description:
Icon is a same-origin URL of the verified immutable icon of this
generation. It is absent when the manifest declares none.

id.description:
ID is the addon identifier and Name its stable machine name. They are
the same in version one: the receipt records no separate catalog name.

mainPage.description:
MainPage is the path the Open action navigates to. It is present only
for an enabled addon whose manifest declares a main page that is one of
its pages.

shadows.description: Shadows lists the built-in chat tools the add-on replaces (bash, say).

skillShadows.description: SkillShadows lists the built-in skills the add-on replaces (xlsx, say).

skills.description:
Skills are the skills the package ships, from the verified manifest.
The owner copies their files into the chats' skill layer.

state.description:
State is running, starting, failed or stopped: the observation of the
process, never an update.

title.description:
Title and Description are the default-language text of the manifest.
Titles and Descriptions carry every language when the manifest
localizes the text, keyed by BCP 47 tag; they are absent otherwise.

toolDefinitions.description:
ToolDefinitions are the model-facing definitions the manifest declares:
the argument schema and the kind of each tool. The host serves them to
chat from the verified manifest; the add-on process is never asked.

tools.description:
Tools are the tool names of the manifest, at most 32. ToolCount is the
full number. The manifest carries no tool descriptions.

ui.description:
UI describes what the shell loads for this app. It is present only for
an enabled addon with a UI whose installed package has a sha256 digest.

update.description:
Update is update-pending when the owner's cached update check says an
update is available for the installed package. It is a separate
observation from State and is absent otherwise: an unchecked, failed
or up to date add-on has none. The list never reaches a library.

icon.description:
Icon is a host icon name, or the empty string when the action uses the
packaged icon of the app (see the icon of the app).

id.description: ID is the manifest identifier of the action.

label.description:
Label is the default-language text; Labels carries every language when
the manifest localizes it.

packagedIcon.description: PackagedIcon is true when the action draws the packaged app icon.

tool.description:
Tool is the own tool the action calls, or Component the exported
component it opens. Exactly one is set.

extensions.description: Extensions are set for a files.preview slot: the file extensions it handles.

generation.description: Generation is the installed generation the caller saw in the list.

operationId.description:
OperationID names the lifecycle operation. Repeating it never runs the
change twice and, after an outcome_unknown answer, it is the identifier
to poll.

actions.description:
Actions are the chat actions that declare a placement and a target.
Slots and Renderers are the other declared contributions. The manifest
was validated at install: every tool named here is a tool of the addon,
every slot is a host slot and every icon is a host icon name or the
packaged icon. The host draws them only while the addon is enabled and
usable by the caller.

css.description: CSS are the URLs of the declared style sheets.

entry.description:
Entry is the URL of the packaged ES module. Every asset URL names the
package digest, so a new package is a new URL.

pages.description:
Pages, Navigation and ChatActions are the identifiers the manifest
declares. The host decides where each one is shown.

sdk.description: SDK is the range of host SDK versions the module accepts.

installedVersion.description: InstalledVersion and InstalledDigest are what metadata.json pins.

signed.description:
Signed says the library requires a signature, so the install of the
update has a verifying step.

sourceId.description: SourceID is the library the backend came from.

version.description:
Version and Digest are the build the library lists now. Version is what
an install of the update names.

failed.description:
Failed is true when the latest fetch failed; the previous releases are
not served in that case.

skipped.description: Skipped and SkippedKinds are as in RefreshResult.

identityRegex.description:
IdentityRegex is an anchored pattern for the signer identity, used
instead of Identity so that master and tagged builds both verify. Only a
library that serves backends may use it; an add-on install refuses it.

artifact_verification.description:
ArtifactVerification overrides Verification only for the gallery OCI artifact.
Backend images keep their separate Verification policy.

library.description:
Library says the URL is a model library (the shared library entry
shape), not a gallery index.

mirrors.description:
Mirrors are tried in order when URL cannot be fetched. They are a
fallback for availability, not a load-balancing pool: the primary is
always preferred, and a mirror is only consulted after the one before
it fails. Any URI the gallery loader understands works here
(https://, github:, file://, oci://).

not_before.description: NotBefore is an RFC3339 timestamp. Empty disables the time check.

source_repository.description:
SourceRepository is an https URL compared exactly against the
certificate's source-repository extension. Empty skips the check.

name.description:
Name is the skill's name and the name of its folder. A plain skill is
named after the add-on: the add-on ID, or the ID and a dash and more
(office-quickstart), so two add-ons never ship one plain name. A skill
that replaces a built-in one has the built-in's name (see Shadows).

shadows.description:
Shadows names the built-in skill this skill replaces. It must equal Name
and be one of ReplaceableSkills. It repeats the name on purpose: the
replacement is an explicit act, which the install warning and the check
read from the manifest without opening the package. Empty: a plain
add-on skill.

description.description: Description is plain text for the model.

inputSchema.description:
InputSchema is the JSON schema of the arguments object. It is an
object schema with explicit properties, additionalProperties false at
the top level and the keywords the host allows only.

kind.description: Kind is read, write, schema or create.

shadows.description:
Shadows names a built-in chat tool that this tool replaces. When the
add-on is installed, running and on for a chat, the model sees one tool
under that name, served by the add-on, and the built-in one is hidden.
Only a name in ReplaceableTools may be shadowed. A tool without it keeps
its add-on name (addon__<id>__<tool>).

uiOnly.description:
UIOnly marks a tool that only the add-on's own page may call, such as a
settings change that asks the host whether the caller is an
administrator. It is never offered to a model, a chat or an agent. The
page has no resource to name, so it must be a read tool without one.

backend.description:
Backend is the resolved backend engine for this model (e.g. "llama-cpp").
Populated at load time from overrides, inline config, or the URL-referenced config file.

files.description: AdditionalFiles are used to add additional files to the model

gallery.description: Gallery is a reference to the gallery which contains the model

installed.description: Installed is used to indicate if the model is installed or not

sha256.description:
SHA256 is the expected sha256 of the backend tarball at URI / Mirrors.
Empty disables the integrity check; OCI URIs carry their own digest.

size.description:
Size is an optional hardcoded model size string (e.g. "500MB", "14.5GB").
Used when the size cannot be estimated automatically.

operation reports it, so a client can tell its own request from

expiresAt.description: ExpiresAt is when the artifact stops being served and is removed.

ageSeconds.description:

userId.description: UserID is the immutable account identifier of the grantee.

state.description: State is pending, committed, rejected or unknown.

tool.description:
Tool and RequestHash name the request the operation ID was first
used for, as the host recorded it when it dispatched the change (kind
apply only). They are absent when the host no longer holds the
request, for example after a restart. Compare RequestHash with the
hash of your own request before you believe a committed state.

proposals.description:
Proposals are the caller's own proposals that still wait for a human
decision, newest first. A proposal of another user is never listed.

arguments.description:
Arguments are the canonical stored arguments. They are the only
arguments that can ever be submitted for this proposal.

blocked.description:
Blocked reports that another operation on the resource has an
unresolved outcome, so confirming is denied until it is resolved. The
operation itself belongs to its proposer and is shown only to the
resource's owner role, in the unresolved listing and in the denial.

digest.description: Digest binds a confirmation to exactly what was shown.

id.description:
ID is the proposal identifier. It is the operation identifier of the
stored operation, so a lost reply is always resolved by the same ID.

reason.description: Reason says why a proposal is cancelled, expired or rejected.

receipt.description: Receipt is present once the runtime answered.

resolution.description:
Resolution is present once the resource owner stopped waiting for an
unresolved outcome. It stays after a late receipt is recorded.

revision.description:
Revision is the schema and data revision the preview saw. The runtime
refuses the apply when it moved.

count.description: Count is the exact number of effects the operation would have.

sample.description:
Sample is a bounded excerpt of the effects, or the whole preview summary
when the addon did not separate one.

actorId.description: ActorID is the resource owner who acknowledged the unknown outcome.

at.description: At is when the acknowledgement was recorded.

reason.description: Reason is the owner's stated reason.

digest.description:
Digest names the installed package an asset belongs to: the lower-case
hex of its sha256. Only the kind "asset" uses it.

revision.description:
Revision is the revision the caller listed. A moved revision is a
stale denial and nothing is changed.

id.description: ID is the opaque resource identifier.

name.description:
Name is the display name the add-on reported. It is empty when the
add-on could not answer in time.

owner.description:
Owner is the display name of the owner, shown to people the resource
is shared with. It is empty in local-owner mode.

revision.description:
Revision is the schema and data revision the listing saw. It is
present for the owner role and goes back with a rename or a delete.

role.description: Role is the caller's own role: viewer, editor or owner.

sharedWith.description:
SharedWith is the number of people the resource is shared with. It is
present for the owner role only.

generation.description:
Generation is the installed generation the listing saw. Rename, delete
and create carry it; a stale tab is denied.

noun.description: Noun is the singular word the add-on uses for its resources.

operations.description: Operations lists the management operations the add-on supports.

sharing.description: Sharing is false in local-owner mode, where nothing can be shared.

truncated.description: Truncated says more resources exist than the bound lists.

resourceId.description:
ResourceID is the resource to use in the conversation. The caller must
hold at least the viewer role on it now.

operationId.description:
OperationID is optional. It is returned with outcome_unknown, and the
change is safe to repeat.

role.description: Role is viewer or editor. The owner role cannot be granted.

generation.description: Generation is the installed generation the caller listed.

operationId.description:
OperationID names the undo. Repeating it with the same change returns
the same result and undoes once; after outcome_unknown it is what to
repeat.

deleted.description:
Deleted is true when the undo removed the resource itself: the change
was its creation.

revision.description: Revision is the revision after the undo.

summary.description: Summary says in one line what the undo did.

conflict.description: Conflict explains how this source clashes with another one, when it does.

enabled.description:
Enabled is what the host does with the source: false for a source that
is turned off, removed, or a shipped default while the official
libraries are off. Suspended tells the last case apart.

mirrors.description: Mirrors are the fallback addresses of the source, in order.

name.description: Name is the backend name of the entry.

sourceId.description: SourceID is the library the entry comes from.

version.description: Version is the version or the channel of the entry.

force.description:
Force reinstalls the backend even when it is already installed and
runnable. Off by default so apply stays idempotent for supervising
apps that ensure their backend on every boot.

backend.description:
Backend is the resolved backend engine for this model (e.g. "llama-cpp").
Populated at load time from overrides, inline config, or the URL-referenced config file.

config_file.description: config_file is read in the situation where URL is blank - and therefore this is a base config.

files.description: AdditionalFiles are used to add additional files to the model

gallery.description: Gallery is a reference to the gallery which contains the model

installed.description: Installed is used to indicate if the model is installed or not

overrides.description: Overrides are used to override the configuration of the model located at URL

size.description:
Size is an optional hardcoded model size string (e.g. "500MB", "14.5GB").
Used when the size cannot be estimated automatically.

variant.description:
Variant installs one specific build of an entry that declares variants,
named as it appears in the entry's `variants` list (see the `variants`
and `auto_variant` fields of the gallery listing). Leave it empty to let
LocalAI auto-select the largest build this host can actually run.

variants.description:
Variants is an optional, UNORDERED list of alternative builds of the same
model (other backends such as MLX or vLLM, other quantizations) that the
installer may pick instead of this entry's own payload. Authoring is
deliberately dumb: name the models, and the selector works out which one
this host should get.

The entry itself is always the last resort, so an entry carrying variants
stays a complete, installable entry and older LocalAI releases, which drop
this key, install it exactly as before.

model_exports.description:
ModelExports is false only when this instance does not see the models
path of the add-on owner. It is the same value as the model_exports key
of GET /api/features.

value.description: Value is the new per-model replica cap on this node. Must be >= 1.
Value is the VRAM cap ("80%" or "12GB"). Empty string clears the cap.

address.description: gRPC address for this replica's backend process

backend_type.description: e.g. "llama-cpp"; used by reconciler to replicate loads

in_flight.description: number of active requests on this replica

family.description: embedding space of the encoder; empty when the backend cannot tell

speaker_encoder.description: trusted metadata from the loaded server encoder, never request data

mode.description: Mode and Version are the ownership mode and package version it holds.

pinned.description: Pinned is set while the backup is the recovery copy of an upgrade.

mode.description: Mode and Version are the ownership mode and package version it holds.

pinned.description: Pinned is set while the backup is the recovery copy of an upgrade.

backups.description: Backups are the backups of the add-on.

data.description:
Data is the add-on's data directory and the owner's records of its
resources, grants and conversation selections.

recoveryCopies.description:
RecoveryCopies are the data copies that restores and failed upgrades
set aside.

lostWrites.description:
LostWrites counts the operations applied after the backup. Their
effects are gone from the data.

previousCopy.description:
PreviousCopy names the directory that holds the data that was replaced.
It stays until an administrator purges it.

historyTruncated.description:
HistoryTruncated says the record of lowered access may have lost
entries older than the backup, so no grant of the backup was restored.

proposalsCancelled.description:
ProposalsCancelled and ProposalsUnknown are the proposals of the add-on
that no longer can be confirmed, and the ones whose outcome is looked up
by receipt and never applied again.

revoked.description:
Revoked counts grants dropped or lowered because access was taken away
after the backup.

mode.description: Mode is the ownership mode of the owner: named-user or local-owner.

operations.description:
Operations lists the operation IDs whose result is recorded, so a
caller that lost an answer can see that its request ran.

phase.description: Phase is the phase of an upgrade or restore in progress.

previousCopies.description: PreviousCopies counts the data copies a restore set aside.

recoveryBackup.description: RecoveryBackup names the copy to restore from.

retention.description: Retention is the policy applied to the backups.

thinking.description:
Thinking gates extended-thinking output. We only surface thinking
content blocks when the client explicitly opts in, matching Anthropic's
API where thinking is off unless requested.

commands.description:
Commands says whether the chat can run commands and code at its next
turn: available, off (the add-on that runs them is switched off for this
chat or not named by its agent), unavailable (installed, but it cannot run
them on this server) or none (no add-on that runs them is installed for
the user).

commands_consent.description:
CommandsConsent is ask when each command of the built-in bash waits for
a yes in the chat.

commands_isolation.description:
CommandsIsolation is isolated (a sandbox) or host (directly on this
machine, with its files and network), when Commands is available.

commands_provider.description:
CommandsProvider serves bash, when Commands is available: builtin (the
built-in bash on this machine) or the ID of the add-on.

commands_reason.description: CommandsReason is why commands cannot run, when Commands is unavailable.

active.description:
Active is false when the add-on that serves the binding is not running. The
binding is kept and works once the add-on is installed.

conversation.description:
Conversation says which chat a message belongs to: sender (one chat
per sender and per platform thread), chat (one chat per group, channel
or direct chat), window (sender, and a new chat after window_minutes
without a message) or thread (a new chat per message; a reply to an
answer goes on in its chat).

reason.description: Reason says in plain words why the binding is not active.

reply_mode.description:
ReplyMode is what a sender sees while a turn runs: off (typing, then
the answer), progress (a working message that names the tools as they
start) or stream (a working message that shows the answer as it is
written). The answer replaces the working message.

send_files.description:
SendFiles sends the files that a turn makes to the sender, after the
answer.

last_run.description:
LastRun is the newest run, if any, and LastDone the end of the newest
run that finished without an error.

min_gap_seconds.description: MinGapSeconds is the shortest time between two runs of a file trigger.

plan.description:
Plan says what a run reads and writes and which Home widget shows the
file it writes; Cost what a run costs.

summary.description:
Summary says when it runs in plain words. NextRun is set for a schedule
trigger that is on.

total.description:
Total, Failed and Running count every run of the agent among your newest
5,000 chats, not only the ones listed.

warnings.description:
Warnings say what the import changed: a model this server does not have
or you may not use is dropped, and a name you already use gets a number.

last_turn.description: LastTurn is how its last turn ended: done, stopped, failed or interrupted.

origin.description:
Origin is empty for a chat you had with the agent, trigger or connector
for one that started by itself; OriginID names the trigger or binding.

missing.description: Missing is true when the file is no longer in your files.

path.description:
Path is the file's path inside your home, for the files API
(GET /api/chats/files/content?path=). It follows a rename of the chat's
folder.

version.description: Version is the version of the file that the message carried.

imported.description:
Imported chats are new. Skipped ones were there already, or have no
creation date or no message to import. Failed ones could not be stored.

opt_in.description:
OptIn says that the group is off until the chat switches it on with
"on" (saved_agents).

provider.description:
Provider is "builtin" when LocalAI serves the tools itself, the ID of
the add-on that serves them in this chat when one shadows them, or
"mixed" when the tools have different providers.

providers.description: Providers says who serves each tool, by tool name.

usable.description:
Usable is false when the group cannot serve this chat now; Reason says
why.

candidates.description:
Candidates are the add-ons that replace it, by ID, and Titles their
titles; Pinned the one chosen in chats_tool_providers.

note.description:
Note says why the built-in serves although an add-on replaces it, or is
empty: the chosen add-on is not running.

provider.description: Provider serves it now: builtin or an add-on's ID.

on.description:
On lists the opt-in groups the chat switches on (saved_agents). Omit
it to keep them as they are.

candidates.description: Candidates are the add-ons that replace it; Pinned the one chosen.

group.description: Group is the per-chat switch group (web), or empty.

mode.description: Mode is chats_host_exec as it applies (bash only): off, ask or on.

provider.description: Provider serves it now: builtin, an add-on's ID, or empty for nothing.

read_only.description:
ReadOnly says the tool only reads; Replaceable that an add-on tool may
replace it by declaring shadows with its name.

setting.description:
Setting is the runtime setting that switches it off; Options are the
other runtime settings that configure it.

unavailable.description: Unavailable says why this server cannot run the built-in, or is empty.

changed.description: Changed is true when the chat changed a file it did not create.

media.description:
Media is true for an attachment that the model received as an image
or a video inside its message.

origin.description:
Origin is "user" (attached by the user or put in the chat folder),
"model" (written by the model in the sandbox) or "tool" (written by a
host tool of the chat, such as write_file).

path.description:
Path is the current path in the user's files ("/" is the home folder),
for the files API. GuestPath is the path the model's tools use.

turn.description: Turn is the turn that brought the file in; 0 when not known.

folder.description:
Folder is the guest path of the chat folder; empty until a file is
attached. FolderPath is the same folder in the user's files.

stale.description:
Stale are old chat folder paths that earlier messages name, such as
the folder's name before a rename. The model is told the new one.

in_title.description: InTitle is true when the title matches.

seq.description: Seq is the first matching transcript line, or 0 when only the title matches.

snippet.description: Snippet is the matching text with a little around it.

active.description:
Active is false when the add-on that serves the binding is not running. The
binding is kept and works once the add-on is installed.

conversation.description:
Conversation says which chat a message belongs to: sender (one chat
per sender and per platform thread), chat (one chat per group, channel
or direct chat), window (sender, and a new chat after window_minutes
without a message) or thread (a new chat per message; a reply to an
answer goes on in its chat).

reason.description: Reason says in plain words why the binding is not active.

reply_mode.description:
ReplyMode is what a sender sees while a turn runs: off (typing, then
the answer), progress (a working message that names the tools as they
start) or stream (a working message that shows the answer as it is
written). The answer replaces the working message.

send_files.description:
SendFiles sends the files that a turn makes to the sender, after the
answer.

page.description: Page is the add-on page that adds and edits bindings of this kind.

confirm_accept_any.description:
ConfirmAcceptAny must be the exact text "accept any message" in the
request that turns accept_any on (a create with accept_any, or an update
that changes it from off to on). Anyone who can message the bot then uses
the agent's tools as you, so the server asks you to say you mean it.

conversation.description: Conversation is sender, chat, window or thread; empty means sender.

kind.description:
Kind is the platform, such as telegram. It is used to create a binding and
ignored by an update. Empty means telegram.

reply_mode.description: ReplyMode is off, progress or stream; empty means progress.

send_files.description:
SendFiles turns the sending of a turn's files on or off. Absent means
on for a new binding and unchanged for an update.

window_minutes.description: WindowMinutes is the time window of the window mode, 1 to 10080.

agent_id.description:
AgentID is the saved agent the chat runs with. Origin is trigger or
connector for a chat that started by itself, and OriginID names the trigger
or binding.

assistant.description: Assistant is true for a chat that has the LocalAI management tools.

running.description:
Running is true while a turn runs. LastTurn is how the last finished turn
ended: done, stopped, failed or interrupted.

settings.description: Settings are the chat's own model settings, when it has any.

agent_id.description:
AgentID is the saved agent the chat runs with. Origin is trigger or
connector for a chat that started by itself, and OriginID names the trigger
or binding.

assistant.description: Assistant is true for a chat that has the LocalAI management tools.

host_consent.description:
HostConsent is the card of a command of the built-in bash that waits for
a yes while a turn runs; answer it with POST /api/chats/{id}/host-exec/consent.

running.description:
Running is true while a turn runs. LastTurn is how the last finished turn
ended: done, stopped, failed or interrupted.

settings.description: Settings are the chat's own model settings, when it has any.

files.description: Files is false when the workspace is off; FilesReason then says why.

image_model.description:
ImageModel is the model that describes the images of a chat whose own
model cannot look at them. It is empty when no model can.

persistent.description:
Persistent is false when conversations live in memory and are lost when
the server restarts.

done.description: Done says a conversion ran at least once.

totals.description: Totals is set for an administrator: the counts of all users together.

kind.description: Kind is agent, trigger, skill, chat or connector.

reason.description: Reason names what was dropped or what went wrong. It holds no secret.

status.description: Status is converted, skipped, failed or dropped.

agent_id.description:
AgentID starts the chat with one of your saved agents. The agent's model,
when it has one, replaces Model, which is then optional.

assistant.description:
Assistant starts the chat with the LocalAI management tools (install
models and backends, change settings). It needs an administrator and the
assistant setting on, and it cannot be combined with AgentID.

model.description: Model is the model the conversation talks to. It cannot change later.

title.description: Title is optional; the conversation is named after its first message otherwise.

before.description: Before and After are context sizes in tokens, for compacted.

code.description:
Code, Model, Retry and Detail say why a turn failed (error only). Code
is a stable name of the cause, such as model_backend_missing; Model names
the model it is about; Retry is the seconds until a model in cooldown
loads again; Detail is the error text without addresses and secrets.

ids.description:
IDs names the messages of pending_delivered, the conversation of
sub_agent_started and sub_agent_done, or the proposal of trigger_proposed.

tool.description: Tool is set for tool_start and tool_end.

usage.description: Usage is set on usage events: what one model request used.

conflict_of.description:
ConflictOf is set when an upload kept both files: it is the path the
caller asked for, and Path is where the new content went.

managed.description:
Managed is set on a path LocalAI manages: "localai" for the LocalAI
folder and the settings files in it, "chats" for the Chats folder.

truncated.description:
Truncated is set when a document or presentation had more text than
the preview keeps.

from_seq.description: FromSeq is the last transcript line to copy; 0 copies everything.

title.description: Title names the new chat; it defaults to the old title and "(fork)".

model.description: Model replaces the model of the file. It is needed when the file names none.

arguments.description: Arguments is a JSON object, at most 16 KiB.

server.description: Server is "connector:<id>" or the name of an MCP server of the chat's model.

tool.description: Tool is a tool of that server whose visibility includes "app".

html.description:
HTML is the page. It must run in a sandboxed frame with no access to the
origin of the interface.

meta.description:
Meta is the ui metadata of the resource as the MCP Apps specification
names it, cleaned: csp (connectDomains, resourceDomains, frameDomains and
baseUriDomains hold only https or wss origins), permissions and prefersBorder.

app.description:
App is set on a tool line whose tool has an MCP App: the interactive page
that goes with the result.

attachments.description: Attachments are the files of a user line.

card.description:
Card is set on a tool line that points at a record, such as a trigger
proposal (kind trigger_proposal, id the proposal's id).

dur_ms.description: DurMs is how long the model thought, for reasoning lines.

rev.description:
Rev is the change set of a checkpoint line, whose text lists the paths
it changed inside your home, one a line. POST /api/chats/files/undo
{rev} undoes it.

role.description: user, assistant, tool, checkpoint or reasoning

text.description:
Text is what was written. For a user line it is the text you typed:
the files you attached are in Attachments.

context.description:
Context adds MCP prompts and resources to this message as context. Each
is expanded on the server, as you, from a server the chat can use.

context_size.description:
ContextSize is the context window in tokens that the loop plans with
(when it compacts the conversation), 0 for the model's own.

reasoning_effort.description: ReasoningEffort is none, minimal, low, medium or high.

system_prompt.description: SystemPrompt is added to the chat's instructions, before the saved agent's.

top_p.description: TopP is above 0 and at most 1.

addon.description:
Addon and AddonTitle name the add-on that provides a skill of the addon
layer.

editable.description: Editable is true when you may change or delete it here.

enabled.description: Enabled is false when the chat has switched it off.

fallback.description:
Fallback is set on a built-in skill that serves because the add-on
skill that replaces it is off or not running in the chat: the title of
that add-on.

id.description:
ID is "layer:name". A switch with the ID turns off the skill of that
layer; a switch with the plain name turns off the skill that wins.

invalid.description: Invalid says why a SKILL.md was skipped.

layer.description:
Layer is where it comes from: folder (a .skills folder of your files),
personal, shared, addon (an installed add-on ships it) or builtin.

path.description: Path is the path of its SKILL.md as the model sees it.

shadowed.description: Shadowed names the layer of a nearer skill with the same name, which wins.

shadowed_by.description:
ShadowedBy is the add-on whose skill wins over this one, when the
winner ships with an add-on (a built-in skill an add-on replaces, or
the skill of an add-on that is not the chosen one).

notes.description: Notes say what could not be read or searched.

running.description:
Running is true while the run's turn is going. LastTurn is how its last
turn ended: done, stopped, failed or interrupted.

background_limit.description: BackgroundLimit is how many a chat may run in the background at once.

running.description: Running is how many of them run now, on any frontend of the server.

cut.description: Cut says that the input or the result was too large and is left out.

input.description: Input is the arguments of the call, at most 16 KiB.

resource_uri.description: ResourceURI is the ui:// resource that holds the page.

result.description: Result is the full MCP result of the call, at most 256 KiB.

server.description:
Server is "connector:<id>" for one of your connectors, or the name of an
MCP server of the model.

tool.description: Tool is the name of the tool on that server.

visibility.description: Visibility is who may call the tool: "model", "app" or both.

app.description:
App is the reference of the MCP App of the call, on tool_end. It has no
input and no result: read the transcript line for them.

card.description: Card is the record the result points at, on tool_end; see ChatsMessage.

seq.description:
Seq is the sequence number of the call's transcript line, on tool_end. A
client that wants the app's input and result reads that one line with
GET /api/chats/{id}/messages?after=<seq-1>&limit=1.

off.description: Off is the list of MCP switches in force.

last_run.description:
LastRun is the newest run, if any, and LastDone the end of the newest
run that finished without an error.

min_gap_seconds.description: MinGapSeconds is the shortest time between two runs of a file trigger.

plan.description:
Plan says what a run reads and writes and which Home widget shows the
file it writes; Cost what a run costs.

summary.description:
Summary says when it runs in plain words. NextRun is set for a schedule
trigger that is on.

average_tokens.description:
AverageTokens is the mean of the last finished runs that reported their
tokens, and Runs how many runs that is.

estimated_tokens.description: EstimatedTokens is the estimate of the proposal; 0 is unknown.

max_runs_per_day.description:
MaxRunsPerDay is the most runs one day can have: the daily limit, or
fewer when the schedule runs less often.

remote.description:
Remote is true when the model runs on a remote service, so the tokens
leave this server.

widget.description: Widget is the id of the Home widget in home.json that shows Writes.

writes.description: Writes is a path in the owner's home, such as data/inbox.json.

tokens.description: Tokens is what the run's model requests used, when it is known.

agent_id.description:
AgentID is optional. Model is needed when neither the agent nor the source
chat names one.

estimated_tokens.description:
EstimatedTokens is about how many tokens one run uses; 0 keeps the
trigger's value.

min_gap_seconds.description:
MinGapSeconds is the shortest time between two runs of a file trigger;
0 keeps the trigger's value (one minute for a new one).

plan.description: Plan describes the runs. An empty field keeps the trigger's value.

model.description: Model moves the chat to another model; the history stays.

settings.description: Settings replaces the chat's settings as a whole.

completion.description: Completion is the number of tokens the request generated.

limit.description: Limit is the context window the loop plans with, 0 when it is not known.

model.description: Model is the model the request used.

node.description:
Node is the worker node that served the request. It is set only when
the server exposes the node header (--expose-node-header).

prompt_ms.description:
PromptMs is the time the backend took to read the prompt, in
milliseconds, when the backend reports it.

tokens_per_second.description: TokensPerSecond is the generation speed, 0 when the backend gave no timing.

used.description: Used is the number of tokens in the context the request sent.

data.description:
Data is the file when it is valid, its last valid version when it is
not (fallback is then true), or an empty object.

prefilled.description:
Prefilled names the keys of data that do not come from the file, and
where they come from ("account").

valid.description: Valid is false when the file breaks its schema; errors says why.

version.description:
Version is what a write sends back in If-Match. It is 0 when the file
does not exist.

chat.description: Chat is the chat that wrote it, and ChatTitle its title when it still exists.

kind.description:
Kind says who made it: user (you, in a form or the Files page), agent
(the assistant), upload or undo.

user_groups.description:
UserGroups holds the collections of the other users. Only an administrator
who asks for all users gets it.

max_results.description:
MaxResults is how many passages to return. A value below 1 picks a
default, and a value above the number of stored passages returns them all.

update_interval.description: UpdateInterval is the minutes between two fetches. Default 60.

choice.description: Choice preserves the selected string or boolean value. Swagger 2 uses a loose object placeholder for this union.

value.description: Value is a string or boolean choice. Swagger 2 uses a loose object placeholder for this union.
Value is a string or boolean for choices, or a zero-based integer for score levels. Swagger 2 uses a loose object placeholder for this union.

input.description: Input is a text string or an array of user messages. Swagger 2 uses a loose object placeholder for this union.

image.description: URL or base64-encoded image to analyze

include_sky.description: return the per-pixel sky map (mono models)

points_conf_thresh.description: keep points with confidence >= this threshold

export_paths.description: paths written for the requested exports

image.description: URL or base64-encoded image to analyze

tokens.description: token IDs to convert back to text

sounds.description:
Sounds is present only when the request set include_sounds. An empty
list then means the model ran and heard no event; omitzero keeps a nil
list (not requested) out of the payload while an empty one stays.

name.description:
Name is the registered speaker this segment was matched to, and NameScore
the cosine similarity of the match. Both are omitted when the backend did
not identify the speaker. Speaker stays the normalized SPEAKER_NN label.

instrumental.description: Simple mode: use text as description; optional instrumental / vocal_language

is_real.description: Liveness fields — see FaceVerifyResponse for why these are pointers.

registered_at.description: original enrollment time when replaying a saved embedding

store.description: vector store model; empty = local-store default

img1_is_real.description:
Liveness fields are only populated when the request set
anti_spoofing=true. Pointers keep them fully absent from the
JSON response otherwise, so callers can tell "not checked"
apart from "checked and fake" (which would collapse to zero
values with plain bool+omitempty).

max_context.description: cap on history used; 0 = model default

id.description: echoed back in the matching result

known_categorical.description: KnownCategorical is [C][T+H]: integer category codes for the future too.

known_covariates.description: KnownCovariates is [C][T+H]: numeric covariates known for the future too.

past_categorical.description: PastCategorical is [C][T]: integer category codes for the past.

past_covariates.description: PastCovariates is [C][T]: numeric covariates known only for the past.

index.description: position of the series in the request

values.description: Values is [Q][H]: Values[q][h] is quantile_levels[q] at step h.

attachments.description:
Images, Videos, Audios and Files are the number of attachments the job
was started with; the content is not kept.

traces.description: Execution traces (reasoning, tool calls, tool results)

images.description:
Attachments for the job, as data URIs (data:<mime>;base64,<data>). An
address is not fetched: the server never makes a request on behalf of a
job's caller. They are saved in the owner's files for the job to read.

url.description: URL to poll for job status

installed.description:
Installed is true when the backend is currently present on disk — i.e. it
appears in gallery.ListSystemBackends(systemState). Importer-registered or
curated pref-only backends default to false unless they also show up on
disk. The import form uses this to warn users that submitting an import
may trigger an automatic backend download.

enabled.description: true if logprobs should be returned

function_call.description: A result of a function call

name.description: The message name (used for tools calls)

schema.Model3DRequest.description: 3D asset generation request body. Generation is image-conditioned

image.description: conditioning image: URL, base64, or data URI (required)

seed.description: random seed; <=0 picks a random seed

capabilities.description:
Capabilities are canonical usecase strings (e.g. chat, vision, transcript,
tts, embeddings, image, video) plus the modifiers "tools" and "thinking".

context_size.description:
ContextSize is the effective context window in tokens the backend will
run with: the configured context_size, or the default when unset. 0 means
the value is unknown (e.g. a loose file with no config). Clients can use
this to size their context budget for auto-compaction and pruning.

input_modalities.description: InputModalities is the subset of {text,image,audio,video} the model accepts.

output_modalities.description: OutputModalities is the subset of {text,image,audio,video} the model produces.

loaded.description:
Loaded lists the model names actually resident in memory after the call.
For a pipeline model these are its sub-models, not the pipeline name.

message.description: Message is a short human-readable status ("model loaded", or an error).

cancel_requested.description: CancelRequested is true when an administrator cancelled the attempt.

eta_seconds.description:
ETASeconds is omitted rather than guessed until enough bytes have moved
for the observed rate to mean anything. A confidently wrong ETA on a
twenty-minute wait is worse than none.

job_id.description:
JobID names the load attempt. A cancel must quote it: it is the
precondition that keeps a cancel from hitting a replacement attempt.

last_error.description: LastError is the cause of a failed attempt.

lease_expires_in.description:
LeaseExpiresIn is the seconds left on the owner's lease. It is negative
when the lease already ran out, which means the owner is gone.

retry_after.description: RetryAfter is the seconds until a new load may start, for a failed attempt.

stopping.description:
Stopping is true while the remote work of a failed attempt is not yet
confirmed ended. StopDeadline is when the model is released regardless.

headers.description: Custom headers for HTTP request (e.g., Authorization)

annotations.description: REQUIRED for output_text - must always be present (use [])

logprobs.description: REQUIRED for output_text - must always be present (use [])

text.description: REQUIRED for output_text - must always be present (even if empty)

completed_at.description: Required: present as number or null

error.description: Always present, null if no error

batch.description: Custom parameters - not present in the OpenAI API

encoding_format.description: Embedding encoding format: "float" (default) or "base64" (OpenAI Node.js SDK default)

files.description: Multiple input images for img2img or inpainting

function_call.description: might be a string or an object

functions.description: A list of available functions to call

grammar.description: A grammar to constrain the LLM output

language.description: Also part of the OpenAI official spec

logit_bias.description: Map of token IDs to bias values (-100 to 100)

logprobs.description:
OpenAI API logprobs parameters
logprobs: boolean - if true, returns log probabilities of each output token
top_logprobs: integer 0-20 - number of most likely tokens to return at each token position

max_completion_tokens.description:
MaxCompletionTokens is the modern alias for max_tokens
(OpenAI deprecated max_tokens; gpt-5 / o-series reject it).
Accepted on the wire so up-to-date clients can use the new
name; the request middleware collapses it into Maxtokens so
internal code reads exactly one field.

messages.description: Messages is read only by chat/completion API calls

n.description: Also part of the OpenAI official spec. use it for returning multiple results

negative_prompt.description:
NegativePrompt for image generation (matches Stable Diffusion WebUI /
vLLM-Omni conventions). Combined, comma-separated, with any "|"-suffixed
negative tags in Prompt.

pooling.description:
Pooling is a LocalAI extension for /v1/embeddings: how the backend's
per-token vectors are reduced to a single embedding. "" or "backend"
leaves pooling to the inference backend (the pre-existing behavior);
"mean", "last" and "decayed_mean" pool Go-side from raw per-token
vectors (the backend must run with the "pooling:none" option, which
model configs get automatically when this is set).

pooling_half_life_tokens.description:
PoolingHalfLifeTokens is a LocalAI extension for /v1/embeddings: the
half-life (in tokens) of the "decayed_mean" pooling scheme — a token's
weight halves every this-many positions counting back from the end of
the conversation. Defaults to 256 when unset.

prompt.description: Prompt is read only by completion/image API calls

ref_images.description: Reference images for models that support them (e.g., Flux Kontext)

stream_options.description: StreamOptions opts into OpenAI streaming extensions, e.g. include_usage.

top_logprobs.description: Number of top logprobs per token (0-20)

top_p.description: Common options between all the API calls, part of the OpenAI spec

usage.description:
Usage is intentionally a pointer with omitempty: per the OpenAI
chat-completion streaming spec, intermediate chunks must not carry
a `usage` field. Marshalling a value-typed usage would emit
`"usage":{"prompt_tokens":0,...}` on every chunk and break
OpenAI-SDK consumers that filter on a truthy `result.usage`
(continuedev/continue, Kilo Code, Roo Code, etc.).

input_tokens.description: Fields for image generation API compatibility

timing_prompt_processing.description: Extra timing data, disabled by default as is't not a part of OpenAI specification

allowed_tools.description: Restrict which tools can be invoked

logit_bias.description: OpenAI-compatible extensions (not in Open Responses spec)

top_logprobs.description: Number of top logprobs to return

detectors.description:
Detectors names the detector models to run (NER and/or pattern). Takes
precedence over Model.

model.description:
Model is a consuming model whose effective PII policy (own
pii.detectors, else the instance default detectors; PII must be
enabled) is used when Detectors is empty.

reveal.description:
Reveal includes the per-entity hash_prefix in the response. Honoured
only for admin callers; ignored otherwise. The raw matched value is
never returned regardless.

text.description:
Text is the string to scan. Bounded only by the server's global HTTP
body limit.

chat_id.description:
ChatID is a chat of the user. Empty means the page's own chat, which is
created on first use.

model.description:
Model is the model of a new page chat. Empty takes the model of the
user's most recent chat.

allowed_at.description:
The version you allowed: when, and the size of its index.html and
page.json and the lines of its index.html, to say what changed.

state.description: State is none, allowed (this version) or changed (an earlier version).

author.description:
Author is who wrote the current index.html: "you" or "assistant" for an
own page, "other" for a shared page another account wrote. A shared page
also has AuthorID and AuthorName, the account that last wrote its
index.html.

folder.description:
A shared page has its shared folder (Folder, a workspace path, and
FolderID, the id the shared-pages routes take), whether you may write in
it, the hash of its code (index.html and page.json; a consent is kept
against it) and your consent: none, allowed or changed.

source.description:
Source is "own" for a page in the user's home and "shared" for a page of
a shared folder.

updated_at.description: UpdatedAt and UpdatedBy are the last change to anything in the folder.

base.description:
Base is the version the page read. A file that changed since is kept and
the content goes to a conflict copy. Zero replaces the file.

added.description: Added is how many entries were embedded, persisted, and indexed.

label_counts.description: LabelCounts is the per-label exemplar count after the call.

skipped.description:
Skipped counts entries whose text was already in the corpus —
duplicates are rejected rather than double-weighted.

total.description: Total is the corpus size after the call.

embedding_models.description:
EmbeddingModels lists the embedder fingerprints present in the
persisted corpus; more than one means part of the corpus is
pending re-embedding on the next load.

input.description:
Input is the user-visible prompt text to classify. Required.
Schema-shape extraction (chat-message concatenation, etc.) is
the caller's responsibility — matches the Probe contract used
by the in-band middleware.

router.description:
Router is the name of the router model (a ModelConfig with a
`router:` block). Required.

cache_similarity.description:
CacheSimilarity carries the cosine similarity of the cache hit
(0 when not cached).

cached.description:
Cached is true when the decision came from the L2 embedding
cache rather than a fresh classifier run.

candidate.description:
Candidate is the model that would be routed to. Empty when no
candidate covers Labels AND no fallback is configured.

classifier.description:
Classifier is the classifier name that produced the decision
(e.g. "score").

fallback.description:
Fallback is true when Candidate is the router's configured
fallback because no candidate covered Labels. Lets callers
distinguish "matched" from "fell back" without comparing names.

labels.description: Labels is the set of active policy labels.

latency_ms.description: LatencyMs is the classifier's wall-clock cost.

nearest_similarity.description:
NearestSimilarity is the cosine similarity of the closest KNN
corpus entry — populated by the knn classifier even when the
decision fell back because the probe was out of corpus range.
0 for other classifiers.

neighbors.description:
Neighbors lists the corpus entries the knn classifier retrieved,
by descending similarity, including ones below the similarity
gate. Empty for other classifiers.

router.description: Router echoes the requested router model.

score.description:
Score is the top label's softmax probability (the
classifier-side confidence signal).

id.description: ID is the folder's stable ID. The shared pages use it as folder_id.

members.description: Members is who may use the folder. Only in the administrator's view.

mode.description:
Mode is what you may do in the folder: read or write. Only in your
own list.

pages.description: Pages is how many pages (pages/<name>/index.html) the folder has.

path.description: Path is the folder's workspace path, /shared/<name>.

action.description: Action is create, rename, delete, restore, grant or revoke.

actor.description: Actor is the user who made the change, or "@assistant".

max_folders.description: MaxFolders and MaxMembers are the limits, in the administrator's view.

everyone.description: Everyone is true for the member that stands for every user.

name.description: Name is the user's name; for "@everyone" it is "@everyone".

principal.description: Principal is the user ID, or "@everyone".

undo_rev.description: UndoRev is the change to undo with POST /api/chats/admin/shared-folders/restore.

id.description: restore only: an ID issued by a save for this model

slot.description: slot id, 0 is the first slot

id.description: issued by the save, sent back to restore

message.description: for example the IDs a save pruned

family.description:
Family is the embedding space of the encoder. The server fills it from the
loaded encoder; exported profiles do not carry it and it is not matched.

backend.description:
Backend is the engine serving this model. The loader knows only the ID,
so it is resolved from the model's config; empty when the model was
loaded without one (a loose file, or a config since removed).

process.description:
Process is the backend process serving the model on this host. Absent
when the model has no local process (a distributed worker holds it) or
the process could not be read.

size_vram.description:
SizeVRAM is DRM-accounted resident device memory in bytes. Nil means
the backend process tree has no complete supported reading.

cpu_percent.description:
CPUPercent is the share of the whole host's CPU used since the previous
reading, 0-100. Absent on the first reading of a process.

rss_bytes.description:
RSSBytes is resident host memory. Weights offloaded to a GPU are not
in it.

instructions.description:
Instructions is a free-form, per-request style/voice description. It maps to
the OpenAI `instructions` field and is forwarded to the backend so expressive
TTS models (e.g. Qwen3-TTS CustomVoice/VoiceDesign) can vary tone or designed
voice per request instead of only via the static YAML option.

language.description: (optional) language to use with TTS model

params.description:
Params carries optional, backend-specific per-request generation parameters
(LocalAI extension, e.g. Chatterbox exaggeration/cfg_weight/temperature).

speed.description:
Speed is the OpenAI `speed` field (0.25-4.0). It is a pointer so an
explicit `"speed": 0` (invalid, rejected with 400) is distinguishable
from an omitted field (left at the backend default). It is normalised
into Params["speed"] so it reaches the backend over the same channel as
the other per-request generation parameters.

voice.description: voice audio file or speaker id

agent_id.description:
AgentID is optional: a saved agent of the owner. The job gets only the
agent's grants and instructions, as a chat with that agent would.

cron.description:
Cron and CronParameters are refused: scheduling is done by the triggers of
the chats, which can run a saved agent on a schedule.

enabled.description: Can be disabled without deletion; absent means enabled

model.description:
Model is the model the job talks to. It may be empty when agent_id names a
saved agent that has a model.

multimedia_sources.description: MultimediaSources is refused: it fed the cron jobs, which are triggers now.

webhooks.description:
Webhook configuration (for notifications).
Supports multiple webhook endpoints.
Webhooks can handle both success and failure cases using template variables:
.Job (Job object), .Task (Task object), .Result (if successful),
.Error (if failed), .Status (job status string).

audio.description: raw audio samples as float32 PCM
optional audio paired with this video

fps.description: frame rate of the source frames; 0 means the backend default

frames.description: ordered frame images: URL, base64 or data URI

audio.description: URL or base64 audio for audio-conditioned generation

end_image.description: URL or base64 of the last frame

negative_prompt.description: things to avoid in the output

num_frames.description: total number of frames to generate

prompt.description: text description of the video to generate

ref_audios.description: reference audio clips (WAV); exclusive with start_image/end_image

ref_images.description: reference images (URL, base64 or data URI); exclusive with start_image/end_image

ref_videos.description: reference videos as frame lists; exclusive with start_image/end_image

start_image.description: URL or base64 of the first frame

method.description: HTTP method (POST, PUT, PATCH) - default: POST

kinds.description: Kinds are the kinds of the change sets: user, agent, upload or undo.

revision.description:
Revision is the newest revision of the changes; it is also the event id,
which a client sends back (Last-Event-ID or ?after=) to resume.

available.description: Available is true only for update-available.

checkedAt.description:
CheckedAt is when the status was computed. LastSuccess is when the
library was last read successfully: a failed check keeps it, so the
page can say how old the knowledge is.

error.description: Error is the redacted class of a failed check.

generation.description: Generation is the installed generation the status describes.

reasons.description:
Reasons are the compatibility reasons of an incompatible or
integrity-error status.

sourceId.description:
SourceID, Channel and Selection are the library, channel and
selection the add-on was installed from. They never change by themselves.

stale.description:
Stale is true when the library data or the cached answer is older than
the time to live.

throttled.description:
Throttled is true when an explicit refresh was not performed because
one ran moments ago. The status is then the last one.
